title: Jack Hanma's battle against body dysmorphia in Grappler Baki
summary: NH discusses his own muscle dysmorphia (bigorexia), framing it as an incurable energy that drives lifters and must be collaborated with rather than eliminated. Using Jack Hanma from Grappler Baki as the extreme case, he argues PEDs only reinforce the disorder and steal from the future self, and that the answer is self-discipline and self-love.
claims: NH says he, like many lifters, suffers from muscle dysmorphia (bigorexia), summed up as the persistent feeling 'I am too small'
The obsession with size and strength often stems from feelings of helplessness in early childhood, and is what gets many young men into lifting
Motivation to lift and bigorexia are closely related: motivation may simply be an expression of the dysmorphia, born from comparing yourself to others
Bigorexia is more dangerous than other dysmorphias because its fulfilment seems doable, which keeps you chasing it
Drugs and surgery are only camouflage that push dysmorphia back briefly and strengthen it later
Dysmorphia has no cure: as the body improves the mind's ideal moves with it, so the circle of dissatisfaction never ends
Trying to eliminate the dysmorphic drive is futile; you must collaborate with it because the person you became exists because of it
Dysmorphia is an energy like thirst or sleepiness that must be satisfied periodically through action; neglecting it kills the mind's drive
Dysmorphia turns against you when progress stalls because muscle can only grow so fast; motivation is a fiery form of anxiety
When progress stalls there are three bad responses: ignore the body and overtrain, give up entirely, or take PEDs
PEDs cannot cure muscle dysmorphia, only reinforce it; they are 'liquid training' and the real victim is the future self
Real-life steroid side effects are subtle and slow, which makes them worse: you fall in love with the benefits before the harm appears
Bigorexia has no patience; even if you reach the dream body the mind immediately wants more, so the dream body is a mirage
The solution is self-discipline: filter the dysmorphic voice, neither silencing it nor obeying every order
Bouts of dysmorphia should be accepted as a simple recognition that you have not arrived yet; keep walking toward your goal daily
Dysmorphia is often planted by parents, siblings, teachers and peers who create complexes in us
The only cure for fulfilment through self-destruction is self-love and accepting your body whatever its state
Getting professional help or medication for body dysmorphia is fine if you need it
Jack Hanma personifies advanced bigorexia: he takes steroids for the biggest body possible even at the cost of his life
